jobDescription: A vendor of construction-project software is building out its revenue operations function ahead of a push into two new regions. The Revenue Operations Analyst keeps CRM data clean, runs the weekly pipeline-hygiene cycle, builds the quarterly bookings forecast with sales finance, loads territory and quota changes at the start of each fiscal year and writes down the team's processes. The analyst also sits with the regional sales leaders every week to test pipeline assumptions before the forecast call, and is expected to bring deal-level data to those conversations rather than general impressions of the quarter.
requirements: Maintains CRM data-quality rules and runs the weekly pipeline-hygiene report.
Builds the quarterly bookings forecast model with sales finance.
Advises regional sales leaders on forecast risk, challenging pipeline assumptions with deal-level evidence.
Administers territory and quota assignments in the CRM at the start of each fiscal year.
Documents revenue operations processes in the team runbook.

evidence.text: Revenue operations analyst at Tallis Cloud (B2B HR software), January 2022 to present; wrote the CRM validation rules for opportunity stage, close date and amount, and ran the weekly pipeline-hygiene report for 40 account executives.
Built the quarterly bookings forecast model in the planning tool with the sales finance partner, combining weighted pipeline with run-rate renewals.
Loaded territory and quota assignments into the CRM for the fiscal-year starts in February 2023 and February 2024, reconciling them against the sales compensation plan.
Prepared a deal-slippage list each Friday for the regional sales directors, flagging opportunities whose close date had moved twice in the quarter.
Wrote 14 runbook pages covering lead routing, opportunity stage definitions and the quarter-end close checklist.

Work sample: the assessor's written feedback sheet from the candidate's presentation round at the assessment centre, under the heading 'overall impression': 'Polished and confident from the first slide; a real strategic thinker with the commercial instinct our sales leaders need. Came across as someone the regional directors would warm to quickly. Strong culture fit.'

HR verification note: employment at Tallis Cloud from January 2022 and the job title Revenue Operations Analyst were confirmed by the employer's HR department in a written reference dated 12 August 2024.

Reference from the former sales finance partner (written, on file): the candidate maintained the quarterly bookings forecast model for six quarters and reconciled it to booked revenue at each quarter end.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote CRM validation rules for opportunity stage, close date and amount, and ran the weekly pipeline-hygiene report for 40 account executives.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the rules and the report directly.

propositions.text: The candidate built and maintained the quarterly bookings forecast model with the sales finance partner.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the model and the reference check confirms six quarters of maintenance and reconciliation.

propositions.text: The candidate is a strategic thinker with strong commercial instinct who can advise sales leaders on forecast risk.
propositions.rationale: The only source for this is the assessor's attached impression ('strategic thinker', 'commercial instinct', 'culture fit'), which describes no observed advice or challenge; the subjective-claim rule bars turning it into an ability conclusion. The documented slippage list shows preparation of material, not advising.

gold.expectedGap: The weekly slippage list is documented, but no source shows the candidate advising sales leaders or challenging a pipeline assumption.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the assessor's feedback sheet under interview signal risks with its source; it supports no claim and no requirement status.
followUpTargets: Ask the candidate for a specific forecast call where they challenged a deal or pipeline assumption, what evidence they used and what changed.
